name: South Dakota
overview: South Dakota's 2025 application cycle included an income-tested homeowner property-tax refund alongside assessment freezes, deferral and local relief. The state repealed the property-refund chapter effective July 1, 2026. The advertised 2026 cycle refunds 2025 sales tax.

programs.name: Assessment Freeze for the Elderly and Disabled
programs.ageRule: 65 or older, or disabled; qualifying surviving spouses may continue.
programs.incomeDefinition: Program household income in the previous year.
programs.maximumBenefit: Assessed value above a qualifying base is excluded; tax savings depend on local rates.
programs.formulaSummary: Freezes qualifying dwelling assessment, subject to income, value and occupancy tests.
programs.application: Annual application to county treasurer by April 1.
eligibilityNotes: Prior-year occupancy of at least 200 days.

sources.title: 2025 Department of Revenue property-tax information guide

programs.name: Property Tax Homestead Exemption (deferral)
programs.ageRule: At least 70, or a qualifying surviving spouse.
programs.formulaSummary: Taxes become a lien and must be repaid with interest on transfer; this is a deferral despite its title.
programs.application: Apply annually to county treasurer by April 1.
interactions: Recipients cannot also receive the historical sales/property tax refund.

programs.name: Municipal property-tax relief for elderly and disabled owners
programs.ageRule: 65 or older, or disabled; certain surviving spouses.
programs.formulaSummary: City property-tax reductions require municipal adoption; availability is not statewide.

programs.name: Property Tax Refund for Elderly and Disabled Persons (2025 application cycle; repealed July 1, 2026)
programs.incomeDefinition: Historical program household income includes specified nontaxable receipts and an up-to-$400 deduction for principal-residence property taxes payable in the application year; federal adjusted gross income alone does not establish this amount.
programs.incomeLimits: 2025 application cycle: program household income up to $16,566 for a single-member household or $22,484 for a multiple-member household. These are not the 2026 sales-refund limits.
programs.maximumBenefit: Historical schedule up to 35% of qualified property tax for a single-member household or 55% for a multiple-member household, subject to annual appropriation and proration. No validated dollar entitlement is supplied.
programs.formulaSummary: The historical program applied an income-based percentage to qualified real-property taxes, subject to appropriation and proration. Revenue calculated the sales-tax and property-tax refunds and paid the larger award once.
programs.application: Historical 2025 cycle: May 1–July 1, 2025. The advertised 2026 cycle offers sales-tax refunds; it does not advertise an ongoing property-tax application.
eligibilityNotes: For the historical 2025 cycle, the homeowner must have owned the residence for at least three years or have been a South Dakota resident for at least five years.
The 2025 announcement uses 2024 residency, age/disability and income facts. The historical record does not certify every transitional 2026 property claim.
interactions: Revenue pays the larger eligible sales-tax or property-tax refund once; the two awards are not additive.
programs.programYear: 2025 application cycle; 2024 reference taxes/facts. Chapter 10-18A was repealed July 1, 2026. Transitional 2026 property-claim rights and the precise assessment/payable-year mapping are not certified.

laterChanges: The governor signed 2026 SB 21, enacted as chapter 37, on March 4, 2026. Its repeal of property-refund chapter 10-18A took effect July 1, 2026 under the default effective-date law.

The advertised 2026 application cycle refunds 2025 sales tax. It uses program household-income limits of $17,215 for a single-member household or $23,265 for a multiple-member household, with appropriation-based pro-rata awards capped at $500 or $1,000 respectively. These sales-tax refunds are outside the property/renter-credit comparison.
2026 assessment-freeze income/value thresholds and residency rules differ from 2025 applications.
researchNotes: The identified historical property-refund record covers the 2025 application cycle. Initial source-pass completion does not validate a household award or adjudicate all transitional claims.

SDCL 2-14-18 generally preserves liabilities incurred before repeal unless the repealing act expressly provides otherwise. SB 21 has no specific accrued-claim transition clause; these sources do not settle whether a particular pre-repeal 2026 property claim was an incurred liability.

The historical statute defines tax year as assessment and levy year, while SDCL 10-21-4 makes taxes due January 1 of the following year. The 2025 announcement describes previous-year 2024 taxes/facts; the original claim form and exact assessment/payable-year mapping remain unverified.

The current senior/disability sales-tax refund is separate from the historical property-tax refund. A property-tax or rent deduction in its income test does not make it a property/renter reimbursement.
